title: Ranveer Singh Personally Called Kalyani Priyadarshan to Join Pralay. She Said Yes.
excerpt: Bollywood's hottest star convinced the Lokah actress to make her Hindi debut in a ₹300 crore post-apocalyptic zombie thriller. August shoot confirmed. Here's everything we know.
body:
Sometimes the best casting stories are the simplest ones: a star picks up the phone and makes the pitch himself.

According to a Mid-Day report, **Ranveer Singh** personally reached out to South sensation **Kalyani Priyadarshan** to convince her to come on board for **Pralay** — his upcoming post-apocalyptic zombie thriller directed by **Jai Mehta**. Ranveer, who is also producing the film, reportedly spent considerable time on the call detailing the script's vision and the ambitious scale of the production.

And it worked.

## The Pitch That Changed Her Mind

Kalyani was initially hesitant. Making your much-anticipated Hindi debut in a niche genre like a post-apocalyptic zombie thriller is not exactly the safe move. Most South actresses crossing over pick a romantic drama, a family entertainer — something that lets audiences ease into a new face.

But Ranveer, who clearly does not operate on conventional logic, was convinced that Kalyani's acting depth was essential for the specific character requirements envisioned by the director. He took charge as producer, picked up the phone, and sold her on the vision.

> "Reports suggesting any uncertainty around Pralay are completely baseless. Ranveer and Jai have been in continuous discussions and have firmly locked the script. The project has already moved into pre-production, with the entire team actively gearing up to create a never-before-witnessed gigantic spectacle out of Indian cinema." — Insider connected to the production

The film is now confirmed to **go on floors in August 2026**.

## Why Kalyani

This is not a random casting call. **Kalyani Priyadarshan** — daughter of legendary filmmaker Priyadarshan — is coming off the massive commercial success of **Lokah**, which concluded its theatrical run with a worldwide collection of **₹303.86 crore**. The film showcased her pull among urban audiences, particularly in the South and overseas markets.

She brings something specific to Pralay: a screen presence that reads as both vulnerable and fierce, the kind of performer who can anchor a high-concept genre film without making it feel like an effects reel. Ranveer clearly saw that. And frankly, a fresh pairing between Bollywood's most charismatic leading man and one of the South's most exciting young actresses is the kind of combination that makes the trade sit up.

## India's First Real Zombie Blockbuster?

Let's talk about what Pralay actually is, because this genre has never been attempted at this scale in India.

Directed by **Jai Mehta** (known for his work in the web series space, with the screenplay co-written by *Lootere* writer **Vishal Kapoor**), Pralay is described as a large-scale, VFX-heavy action thriller set in a dystopian, post-apocalyptic world. The budget is reportedly in the range of **₹300 crore** — making it one of the most expensive Hindi films ever mounted.

The zombie genre has produced global franchises: *28 Days Later*, *Train to Busan*, *The Last of Us*, *World War Z*. But mainstream Bollywood has never touched it at this scale. There have been B-grade horror films that flirted with the undead, but nothing that treated the genre with the production value and narrative ambition that Pralay seems to promise.

For Ranveer, it is a deliberate pivot after the franchise-defining success of **Dhurandhar**, which crossed **₹1,200 crore** worldwide. He is not looking to repeat a formula. He is looking to create a new one.

## Pre-Production Is Moving Fast

The production has already entered an intensive pre-production phase: location scouting, concept design, action planning, VFX preparation, and casting formalities are all underway. Earlier rumors about creative differences between Ranveer and Jai Mehta have been firmly dismissed by sources close to the project.

The script is locked. The female lead is locked. August is locked.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For NRI audiences who grew up watching Bollywood comedies and romances, the emergence of a genuinely ambitious genre project like Pralay signals a shift in what Indian cinema thinks it can do. This is not Bollywood borrowing from Hollywood — it is Bollywood building something that could compete with it.

And with Kalyani's addition, it is also a film that bridges the North-South divide in a meaningful way — a Telugu-Malayalam star making her Hindi debut opposite Bollywood's biggest earner, in a genre that has no language barrier.

The zombies are coming. And they are speaking Hindi.
